Let
\[
r=\frac{s}{1+s},\qquad h(r)=g(s).
\]
Then \(r\in(0,1)\), and the differential equation becomes
\[
\bigl(r(1-r)h'(r)\bigr)'+\lambda h(r)=0.
\]
The condition \(s\to0^+\) is \(r\to0^+\), so \(h(0)=1\), and \(s\to\infty\) is \(r\to1^-\), so \(h\) must remain finite at \(r=1\).

Solving by a power series \(h(r)=\sum_{m\ge0}a_mr^m\), \(a_0=1\), gives
\[
(m+1)^2a_{m+1}+\bigl(\lambda-m(m+1)\bigr)a_m=0.
\]
If the series does not terminate, then \(a_m\sim C/m\) with \(C\ne0\), so \(h(r)\) has logarithmic divergence as \(r\to1^-\). Hence finiteness at \(r=1\) forces termination, so
\[
\lambda=n(n+1)
\]
for some integer \(n\ge0\), and \(h\) is the shifted Legendre polynomial
\[
h(r)=P_n(1-2r).
\]
This polynomial has exactly \(n\) zeros in \((0,1)\), so the assumption of exactly two zeros gives \(n=2\). Therefore
\[
g(s)=P_2\!\left(\frac{1-s}{1+s}\right)
=\frac{3\left(\frac{1-s}{1+s}\right)^2-1}{2}
=\frac{s^2-4s+1}{(1+s)^2}.
\]
Since \(s=\log x\),

\[
\boxed{f(x)=\frac{(\log x)^2-4\log x+1}{(1+\log x)^2}}
\]
